text.p: - Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is unlikely to be able to fulfil the tasks set by President Boris Yeltsin in his annual State of the Nation address to be delivered on March 6.
- Bread quality in Russia has been going down steadily since the government abolished a special federal bread quality control inspectorate last year.
- Rumours of an imminent cabinet reshuffle have put pressure on ministers. First Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Ilyushin postpones his visit to Japan.
- Georgia is planning to become a full member of the Caspian oil-producing consortium.
- Changes in the Russian cabinet will most probably be limited in scale and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will keep his post.
- The IMF and World Bank insist Russia changes its pension legislation.
- Trillions of roubles of state pension money are being misused.
- Six new underground stations will be built in Moscow city centre.
